run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubePodNotReady (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 since 2026-11-25T07:45:50Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The KubePodNotReady alert for otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 is explained by an image-pull failure on that pod: the Deployment product-catalog's pod template was changed at 2026-11-25T07:45:11Z to the image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1, which does not exist in the registry. The new ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f created pod xcr42, its init container wait-for-astronomy-db ran successfully, and the product-catalog container has never started: kubelet reports 'failed to resolve reference ... not found', ErrImagePull, and ImagePullBackOff (21 back-off events to 07:50:18). The pod is Pending with Ready=False/ContainersNotReady, kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true"} is 0 from 07:46 through 07:51, and the KubePodNotReady rule (which matches Pending pods) is firing with value 1 and activeAt 2026-11-25T07:45:50Z. The previously created ReplicaSet product-catalog-658dcdbc87 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog) is still running and ready; the Service still lists that pod as a ready address and product-catalog span rate continued at ~13-15 spans/s with no error-status spans observed, so service-level failure was not observed. Only product-catalog carries the nonexistent image; every other otel-demo Deployment keeps its ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-* image with 1 ready replica. The Kubernetes object holding the fault is the Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog; who applied the change (field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator') is not a readable Kubernetes object and remains unknown.

claims.text: Pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 (created 2026-11-25T07:45:11Z, owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f, node kind-environment-worker2) is in phase Pending with Ready=False reason ContainersNotReady; container product-catalog is not ready, restartCount 0, state waiting reason ErrImagePull with message: failed to pull and unpack image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1": failed to resolve reference ... not found.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog currently specifies container image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1 and reports status replicas=2, readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1, unavailableReplicas=1; its managedFieldsSummary shows manager "OpenAPI-Generator" operation Update at 2026-11-25T07:45:11Z (no subresource), i.e. a spec write at that timestamp.

Only Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog was updated by a non-status manager in the incident window: the filtered deployment list over otel-demo shows only product-catalog with manager "OpenAPI-Generator" Update at 2026-11-25T07:45:11Z (checkout and shipping show only kube-controller-manager status updates at 07:44:00Z).

Two ReplicaSets are owned by Deployment product-catalog (uid 2f2cbf06-5842-480d-b1d2-7e4f0dba8a72): product-catalog-658dcdbc87 created 07:42:52Z with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog and readyReplicas 1, and product-catalog-7b499ffb4f created 07:45:11Z with image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1 and no readyReplicas.

Kubelet events for pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 on node kind-environment-worker2: init container wait-for-astronomy-db pulled busybox:latest and started at 07:45:12Z; for spec.containers{product-catalog} there are 5 Failed events "Failed to pull image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1 ... not found" and "Error: ErrImagePull" from 07:45:13Z to 07:48:06Z, and 21 BackOff events "Back-off pulling image ..." / "Error: ImagePullBackOff" from 07:45:14Z to 07:50:18Z.

Pod logs for product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42: container product-catalog has no current log because it "is waiting to start: image can't be pulled"; the only line read is from wait-for-astronomy-db, "astronomy-db (10.96.59.214:5432) open" at 2026-11-25T07:45:12Z.

Prometheus kube-state-metrics confirms non-readiness for this pod: kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true"}=0 and condition="false"=1 for pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 at every 60s sample from 07:46:00Z to 07:51:00Z, and at 07:51:00Z kube_pod_status_phase phase="Pending"=1 with phase="Running"=0 (the sibling pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-27klx has condition true=1, phase Running=1).

The alerting rule "KubePodNotReady" in group kubernetes-apps is firing with labels namespace=otel-demo, pod=product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42, severity=warning, value 1, activeAt 2026-11-25T07:45:50Z; its query sums pods that are in phase Pending|Unknown, or Running with kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true"}==0, restricted to pods with a non-Job owner.

The nonexistent image is unique to product-catalog: a cluster-wide search of Deployments for an image matching "hello-bench" returns only otel-demo/product-catalog, and the otel-demo Deployment listing shows all other deployments on ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-* (plus postgres/valkey/flagd/collector images) with readyReplicas 1 and no unavailableReplicas.

kube_pod_container_info shows the running pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-27klx with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog and image_id ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:7578cbf65fa4f0fc68e077e4f299ecccaa31d9778d407e41ab5973d247fd4b8e, while pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 has only image_spec quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1 and no image_id (no image was ever resolved for it).

The Service product-catalog (ClusterIP, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog) still has the older pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-27klx as a ready address (10.244.2.23 on kind-environment-worker) and lists the failing pod only under notReadyAddresses, so the failing pod was never added to serving endpoints.

product-catalog kept producing spans after the failing pod was created: the 2m rate of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"} is ~13.1-15.5 spans/s at every 60s sample from 07:45:00Z to 07:51:00Z, and the 60m status breakdown for service_name=product-catalog contains only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET (8218.81 span-increases) with no non-UNSET status series, so no product-catalog error-status spans were observed.

Rejected: a general registry/network/DNS problem or a node problem on kind-environment-worker2. The kubelet error is a registry NotFound for the exact reference ("failed to resolve reference ... not found", not a timeout or authorization error), the same node successfully pulled busybox:latest at 07:45:12Z and started the init container, and other otel-demo pods on worker-family nodes are running and ready.

Rejected: a failing readiness/liveness probe on product-catalog. The Ready=False condition message is "containers with unready status: [product-catalog]" with reason ContainersNotReady and the container's state is waiting/ErrImagePull, so the application container never started and no probe could have been evaluated for it.

Rejected: unschedulable pod or insufficient node resources/quota. Pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 has a SuccessfulCreate by ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f and a "Successfully assigned otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42 to kind-environment-worker2" Scheduled event at 07:45:11Z, its PodScheduled condition is True, and its init container ran, so no FailedScheduling or quota shortfall was observed for it.

The image change looks externally applied rather than part of the Helm install: the Deployment's earlier write is manager "helm" Apply at 07:42:52Z with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog, and the later non-status write at 07:45:11Z is manager "OpenAPI-Generator" (an API-client manager name), which coincides with creation of ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f and the bad image; this is consistent with an automated fault/changemanagement patch, but no Kubernetes object identifying that actor was readable.

Revert the product-catalog Deployment container image to a valid reference (for example the previously used ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog) or to a quay.io/it-bench tag that actually exists, then confirm the old ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f pod is replaced and the Deployment reports unavailableReplicas=0; additionally identify the client writing as field manager "OpenAPI-Generator" and add admission/validation so non-existent image references cannot be rolled out.

gaps: Jaeger trace tools failed with HTTP 404 for this target (traces_search for service product-catalog and traces_list_services both returned SOURCE_ERROR/INVALID_PARAMS), so trace-level call-graph and error-detail evidence was not available; only span metrics were used.

The actor behind field manager "OpenAPI-Generator" is not a Kubernetes object in the readable kinds: listing customresourcedefinitions to look for a chaos/fault-injection CRD was refused with RESULT_TOO_LARGE, so a CRD-based injector cannot be confirmed or excluded.

change_history is not an integrated data source for this Run, so when and by what process the Deployment image field was changed cannot be established beyond the managedFieldsSummary timestamp 2026-11-25T07:45:11Z.

A cluster-wide ConfigMap scan for content matching "hello-bench|product-catalog" returned no rows (status no_data), so a ConfigMap-driven image injection could not be confirmed or ruled out from that query.

The running product-catalog pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-27klx returned no error-matching log lines (its product-catalog container stream had 0 lines read), so its internal health is not verified beyond readiness, endpoints membership and span-status metrics.

Non-UNSET span status counts were returned for other services (ad, currency, frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator, recommendation) in the same 60-minute view; no baseline was established and no evidence ties them to this pod's image-pull failure, so they are unassessed and not attributed to this alert.

The alert annotation says non-ready for longer than 15 minutes, but the pod was created at 2026-11-25T07:45:11Z and the rule's activeAt is 2026-11-25T07:45:50Z; the rule view (duration 300s) was read after the authorized window, so its for-duration at incident time is unknown.
next_steps: Restore a valid image reference on Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog and verify the rollout replaces pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xcr42.
Trace the API client/automation writing as field manager "OpenAPI-Generator" at 2026-11-25T07:45:11Z (audit logs are not available in this Run).
Verify whether tag 1.0.0rc1 exists in the quay.io/it-bench repository before any future rollout, and gate non-existent image references via admission policy.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
